summary: Sustained soft 429s after ingress IP NAT pool reuse during high connection churn
description:
Issue summary:
Users on a dedicated pool (FinSight Analytics) started seeing persistent soft 429s during a period of very high short-lived connection churn from their upstream CDN. The 429s begin ~6 minutes after a surge and affect both streaming and short polling clients.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~15% request failure rate (429) for interactive endpoints for a 20-minute window during nightly batch fanout.
- Affects latency-sensitive client facing flows (chat and re-ranker).
- No corresponding spike in token usage or billing; failures are throttles (429) returned by the edge layer.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, us-east ingress (edge pool ep-us-east-3).
- Customer on Dedicated capacity (dedicated GPU pool) behind our hosted API.

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer traffic pattern):
1) Customer orchestrates 10k short-lived client connections from a set of CDN worker IPs; each connection uploads a small prompt and disconnects.
2) CDN reuses a small NAT public IP pool for outbound egress, causing many distinct client sessions to collide on the same NAT addresses.
3) After several minutes of churn, edge starts returning 429s to a subset of requests from that customer.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include header: X-RateLimit-Reason: NAT_REUSE_DETECT and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 (for many requests).
- Rate-limiter logs show per-source-IP token bucket exhaustion followed by a short refill delay; multiple outgoing client sessions appear attributed to the same source IP bucket.
- Token accounting appears to double-count or aggregate unrelated logical sessions when NAT addresses are recycled rapidly.

Expected behavior:
- Rate-limiter should account per-api-key (tenant) and per-route correctly regardless of source IP churn; short-lived connection reuse should not induce tenant-wide soft 429s.

Relevant logs and traces (snippets):
- edge-proxy (ep-us-east-3) logs: "INFO rate_limiter: bucket_exhausted src=54.23.12.99 tenant=finsight key=xxxx route=/v1/chat remaining=0 reason=NAT_REUSE_DETECT"
- gateway traces show a spike in connection teardown/establish events coincident with the 429 window.

Immediate notes:
- This reproduces only when the upstream egress (CDN) reuses a small NAT pool while producing many short-lived TCP/TLS sessions.
- Customers using persistent connections or HTTP/2 multiplexing are not impacted in the same way.

Workaround suggested to customer (applied):
- Switch client to use long-lived connections / HTTP/2 multiplexing where feasible.
- If using CDN workers, request larger NAT pool from CDN provider or enable source IP preservation.
- We temporarily bumped per-route burst allowance for their dedicated route to reduce hard failures while we investigate.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: our rate-limiter has a performance optimization that keys some fast-path accounting by (src_ip, route) for micro-burst protection. That optimization causes collisions when many logical clients share a NAT public IP and create short sessions; the per-ip bucket is exhausted even though tenant-level tokens are still available.
- Replayed a synthetic test from internal lab: spawned 5k short connections through a small NAT pool of 8 addresses -> reproduced soft 429s within ~4 minutes.
- Instrumented code path and confirmed a downstream fallback to per-api-key accounting is present but delayed to avoid added coordination costs; in churn scenarios the fast-path block triggers earlier and returns 429 before fallback completes.
- Correlated with edge-proxy version v2.7.1 which contains the fast-path optimization; v2.8.0 includes a nat-awareness flag and quicker tenant-scope fallback.

Next steps / remediation plan:
1) Short term: keep per-route burst increase for the affected dedicated route and request customer to increase connection pooling. (Done 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC)
2) Deploy edge-proxy v2.8.0 to the affected pool (ep-us-east-3) with nat-awareness flag enabled for the next canary window (scheduled 2026-03-12).
3) Merge and deploy PR that shortens fast-path --> tenant-fallback window to eliminate early 429s when NAT churn is detected (PR referenced below).
4) Post-deploy: run synthetic churn test and coordinate with customer for a controlled surge to validate fix.

Customer communication plan:
- Notified customer (FinSight) on 2026-03-10 about the workaround and planned patch.
- Offer to assist in configuring their CDN for larger NAT pools or connection reuse.

Resolution notes (planned):
- Patch (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2413) reduces the fast-path window and adds a NAT-reuse heuristic to prevent per-ip bucket exhaustion from causing tenant throttles.
- We will rotate affected NAT IP pool as a second short-term mitigation if deployment takes longer than planned.
comments: 2026-03-10T13:45:00Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported intermittent 429s across chat and re-ranker during their nightly fanout. Provided initial logs and timestamps. Escalating to Edge SRE.

2026-03-10T14:20:00Z - Miguel Torres (Edge SRE): Reproduced locally with a small NAT pool. Likely collision between NAT reuse and per-src fast-path in rate-limiter. Marking as Sev1 due to customer impact. Assigning owner and scheduling short-term burst increase.

2026-03-10T15:15:00Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Applied temporary per-route burst increase and informed customer. Customer saw lowered 429 rate but still some errors. Instructed to enable keepalive/HTTP2 if possible.
2026-03-11T09:30:00Z - Grace Liu (Customer Success): Customer asked whether this will affect billing — clarified throttles are not billable errors; provided status update and remediation timeline.
2026-03-12T02:05:00Z - Miguel Torres (Edge SRE): v2.8.0 canary deploy scheduled for ep-us-east-3 at 2026-03-12T10:00Z. PR link and post-deploy validation steps added to the ticket.
investigation_notes: Lab reproduction confirmed. Root cause traced to a fast-path optimization in rate-limiter keyed by source IP that degrades into 429s when the same NAT IP services many short-lived sessions. Confirmed presence in edge-proxy v2.7.1. Solution is to enable nat-aware accounting + faster fallback to tenant-scoped buckets.
resolution_notes: Planned: deploy edge-proxy v2.8.0 with nat-aware flag (PR #2413). Temporary mitigations (per-route burst bump, recommend connection pooling) applied. Post-deploy validation scheduled; if canary passes, rollout to all us-east pools and notify customer.
